name: Gaussian Grounded Inter-Reflection
definition: A technique to model inter-reflection by separating direct light $L_{dir}$ and indirect light $L_{ind}$, approximating visibility $V$ via ray tracing on an extracted mesh to determine occlusion.
summary: Gaussian Grounded Inter-Reflection models indirect illumination in reflective scenes by separating direct and indirect light, using mesh-based ray tracing or SDF ray marching to compute self-occlusion and secondary bounces.
